subject: Immediate: Helios production latency spike & error surge — KV prefetch/caching feedback loop
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia@helios.ai>
To: Helios Support <support@helios.ai>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west)

Team —

We started seeing a sharp spike in response latency around 08:45 PT and a growing rate of 502/503 responses for our inference routes. The client facing service for Helios Chat is degraded; multiple customers have reported timeouts. Attaching a short timeline and a cropped p99 graph.

What we see:
- p50 ~ stable, p95 ~ elevated, p99 jumped from 420ms to >1.8s
- error rate spiked to ~4.1% (mostly 502/503 gateway errors)
- throughput briefly dropped 30% while queue lengths grew

Can you confirm whether this looks like a routing/config problem or something in the KV prefetch/caching layer? We saw references to cache evictions and restart chatter in the logs. This is impacting our customers — would like an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Amelia Ross
Head of Product, Helios AI

Attachments: timeline.txt, p99_latency_timeseries.png

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, amelia@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west)

Amelia — thanks for the heads up and the chart. I'm escalating immediately. Rishi, Laura — can you triage and confirm whether this is a KV cache/prefetch feedback loop or something else? Priority: (1) stabilize Helios traffic, (2) stop 502 spikes, (3) root cause.

Action I'm requesting:
- Rishi: grab recent support bundle and checks on hotkey eviction rates, kv-prefetch queue depth, and backend GPU backpressure metrics.
- Laura: if there's a safe quick mitigation (eviction policy toggle, reduce prefetch depth, or short-term priority lane bump), please outline steps we can run now.
- Ben: heads up to sales/AMs — we may need a customer update and to discuss credits if SLA is missed.

I will be on the war room call at 09:40 PT.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Acct Exec (Enterprise) — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0129

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, amelia@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west)

Quick summary from initial triage (logs + metrics):
- Observed rapid hotkey churn on Helios tenant: a small set of prefixes (~0.6% of keys) account for ~48% of fetches in the last 20m.
- Prefetch agent ramped up aggressively in response to transient traffic patterns; that increased KV eviction churn and constant recomputation of prefetch windows.
- Backend queues in the serving runtime show head-of-line blocking on hosts with high KV miss rates — this aligns with the 502s and the observed drop in throughput.
- We also saw a coupling where higher prefetch concurrency caused KG (KV) locks to hold longer, which cascaded into increased latency for unrelated lanes.

Immediate recommended mitigations (safe and reversible):
1) Flip kv-prefetch concurrency down to 25% of current for Helios tenant (expected immediate reduction in eviction churn).
2) Temporarily enable conservative-LRU eviction on priority lanes for Helios (reduces thrash).
3) Route a fraction (~20%) of Helios traffic to a warmed fallback model variant (lower memory footprint) to reduce pressure while we stabilize.

I can apply (1) and (2) in the next 8–10 minutes and monitor. Will hold on (3) until we confirm.

Logs/attachments: support_bundle_helio_1004.tar.gz (included kv stats + host-level traces).

- Rishi
SRE — Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, amelia@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west)

I'll implement the mitigation steps now and provide a rollback plan. Runbook notes:
- Step A: kv-prefetch concurrency -> set to 25% (live toggle) 
- Step B: set eviction policy to conservative-LRU for Helios priority lane (no restart required)
- Step C: increase priority lane tokens for Helios from 8 -> 12 for 30 minutes to reduce HOL impact
- Monitoring: p99 / 5xx / kv-miss-rate dashboards and job-level queue depth.

Expected outcome: within 5–12 minutes we should see eviction churn decrease and p99 start to fall. If not, escalate to routing fallback to avoid customer impact (Ben please prep customer comms).

Applying Step A & B now. Will update at +10m.

—Laura
Prod Ops Lead — Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: amelia@helios.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, support@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west)

Amelia — I'm sorry for the outage impact. Vanessa and I will own customer comms while ops/SRE stabilize the service. Planned customer update for your stakeholders at 10:30 PT with the following points:
- What happened: transient traffic pattern caused aggressive prefetching which increased KV eviction churn and head-of-line blocking for some hosts.
- What we're doing: lowering prefetch concurrency, switching eviction policy to conservative-LRU for priority lane, and increasing priority tokens temporarily.
- ETA for stabilization: 10–20 minutes (monitoring underway).
- Next steps: full RCA + mitigation plan in 48 hours; if SLA is missed we'll follow Helios contract (we'll coordinate credits).

If you'd like us to include a brief technical blurb for your engineering team, say the word and we will add it.

—Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: amelia@helios.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency increase + 502 errors (region: us-west) — Stabilized / Next steps

Quick post-mortem update (stabilized):
- Timeline: mitigations applied 09:50 PT (prefetch concurrency down, eviction policy toggled, priority tokens bumped).
- Outcome: p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> 480ms within ~12 minutes; 5xx error rate returned to baseline (~0.1%). Throughput normalized. Graph attached (p99_latency_timeseries.png).
- Root cause (preliminary): a looping prefetch pattern triggered by a Helios usage spike combined with a low-sensitivity LRU on priority lanes created eviction churn and long-held KV locks on a subset of hosts. That produced HOL blocking that propagated to other lanes.

Follow-ups / action items:
1) Engineering: schedule a targeted fix (KV prefetch smoothing + backoff) and a config safety check to prevent aggressive concurrency increases for tenants with high prefix skew. (Owner: Rishi, ETA: 48h.)
2) Product/CS: provide Helios with a written RCA and customer-friendly summary. (Owner: Ben / Vanessa, ETA: 24h.)
3) Ops: propose a config guardrail: automated prefetch concurrency cap + automated fallback route to warmed variant when eviction churn above threshold. (Owner: Laura, ETA: 72h.)
4) Exec: I will prepare a one-page briefing for our leadership and Helios execs if we anticipate escalation.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. I uploaded the support bundle and the temp patch we used to the incident folder.

—Vanessa
Acct Exec (Enterprise) — Redwood Inference
Attachments: support_bundle_helio_1004.tar.gz, p99_latency_timeseries.png, kv-policy-diff.patch
